tier_reason: result.json from scc-tw/cryptobench-cpp (harness: src/benchmarks/hash_benchmarks.cpp plus src/adapters/{libsodium,openssl}_adapter.cpp) has BM_Libsodium_BLAKE2b and BM_OpenSSL_BLAKE2b means that match every claimed number exactly. It still falls short of A because the CPU model and the compiler and version are not recorded. It is not B either: this is an obscure personal repo (0 stars, no LICENSE file, last commit 2025-11-05) and one local laptop run, not a well-known independent suite or a peer-reviewed paper, so it is third-party numbers with partial methodology, which is C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: libsodium's BLAKE2b beats OpenSSL's BLAKE2b at small-to-medium sizes (means of 5 repetitions): ~2.70x at 64B (577.8 vs 213.7 MB/s), ~1.91x at 256B (1243.6 vs 650.3 MB/s), ~1.18x at 1024B (1307.0 vs 1107.2 MB/s), about tied at 4096B (1338.4 vs 1333.9 MB/s); OpenSSL retakes the lead by ~4% at 16384B (1402.7 vs 1349.3 MB/s) (all derived from page data)
corrections.compiler_and_flags: The README says -O3 -march=native -mtune=native -flto -funroll-loops -fomit-frame-pointer (PGO optional) is applied to all libraries. However, cmake/FetchLibsodium.cmake configures libsodium with CFLAGS=${CMAKE_C_FLAGS_RELEASE}, not the shared CRYPTO_BENCH_C_FLAGS that OpenSSL gets, so libsodium's flags probably differ. result.json does not record the compiler, its version, or whether PGO was used.
corrections.hardware: Host 'sccdeMacBook-Air.local' (Apple Silicon MacBook Air; the chip model is not named), 8 logical CPUs. The result.json context block reports 64KB L1D / 128KB L1I / 4MB L2, a release build, and a run dated 2025-11-05.
corrections.caveats: This is a harvested shootout result, not a claim libsodium makes about itself. It is a single local run (2025-11-05) on a MacBook Air by the author of an obscure 0-star benchmark repo; the CPU model and compiler are not recorded. The small-size gap is inflated by the harness: the OpenSSL adapter calls EVP_MD_CTX_new, EVP_DigestInit_ex(EVP_blake2b512()) and EVP_MD_CTX_free on every hash, while libsodium makes one crypto_generichash_blake2b call. The 64-256B gains therefore mostly measure OpenSSL EVP per-call overhead rather than the BLAKE2b compression function, and at 16KB OpenSSL is ~4% faster. The README says flags are identical, but the build scripts pass libsodium CMAKE_C_FLAGS_RELEASE rather than the shared -march=native/-flto flags.

notes: All five libsodium and OpenSSL BLAKE2b means in result.json match the record exactly, and the ratios are correct. libsodium metadata checks out: 13,965 stars, last commit 2026-09-22, not archived or a fork, GitHub reports NOASSERTION but the LICENSE file is ISC. The hardware L1D was wrong (64KB, not 32KB). Tier cut from B to C because the suite is not well known. The OpenSSL per-call EVP context allocation makes the small-message win largely an API-overhead artifact.
